name: מנת מספרים מרוכבים בצורה p+qi (באנגלית)

functions.name: igcd2
functions.body: if b=0 then abs(a) else igcd2(b,mod(a,b))

functions.name: texp
functions.body: if constantp(x) and freeof(%i,x) and is(x<0) then sconcat("\\left(",tex1(x),"\\right)") else tex1(x)

functions.name: texnsum
functions.body: block([L:first(args(e))], sconcat(tex1(first(L)), apply(sconcat, map(lambda([t], if constantp(t) and is(t<0) then sconcat("-",tex1(-t)) else sconcat("+",tex1(t))), rest(L)))))

functions.name: rsq
functions.body: block([s,t,nn,dd,aa:1,mm:1,g,u], if ratnump(x) then return(tex1(x)), s: if is(x<0) then "-" else "", t: ratsimp(x^2), nn: num(t), dd: denom(t), for f in ifactors(nn*dd) do (aa: aa*f[1]^floor(f[2]/2), mm: mm*f[1]^mod(f[2],2)), g: igcd2(aa,dd), aa: aa/g, dd: dd/g, u: sconcat(if aa=1 then "" else string(aa), "\\sqrt{", string(mm), "}"), if dd=1 then sconcat(s,u) else sconcat(s,"\\frac{",u,"}{",string(dd),"}"))

functions.name: cxq
functions.body: block([r1:"", i1:""], if p#0 then r1: rsq(p), if q#0 then (i1: if is(abs(q)=1) then "\\mathrm{i}" else sconcat(rsq(abs(q)), "\\mathrm{i}"), i1: if is(q<0) then sconcat("-",i1) else if p#0 then sconcat("+",i1) else i1), if p=0 and q=0 then "0" else sconcat(r1,i1))

questiontext:
Convert the following number into the form \(p+qi\) where \(p\) and \(q\) are real.

\[ \frac{{{CT:0}} + {{CT:1}}i}{{{CT:2}}+{{CT:3}}i} \]

Note: give your answer in the form \(p+qi\), in the box below.

[[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]

How to enter: the imaginary unit \(i\) is typed as the letter i (or %i), and multiplication with a star. For example 3-2*i.
generalfeedback:
Outline: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the denominator; the denominator becomes a real number, and then the real and imaginary parts are divided by it.
Step 1 — Multiply by the conjugate
To remove \(i\) from the denominator, multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the denominator, \({{CT:2}}-{{CT:3}}i\), and expand both products term by term:

\[ \frac{{{CT:0}}+{{CT:1}}i}{{{CT:2}}+{{CT:3}}i}\cdot\frac{{{CT:2}}-{{CT:3}}i}{{{CT:2}}-{{CT:3}}i}=\frac{{{CT:4}}-{{CT:5}}i+{{CT:6}}i-{{CT:7}}i^2}{{{CT:8}}-{{CT:9}}i+{{CT:10}}i-{{CT:11}}i^2} \]

Step 2 — Use \(i^2=-1\)
In the denominator the middle terms cancel, \(-{{CT:9}}i+{{CT:10}}i=0\), and \(-{{CT:11}}i^2=+{{CT:11}}\):

\[ {{CT:8}}+{{CT:11}}={{CT:12}} \]

In the numerator \(-{{CT:7}}i^2=+{{CT:7}}\) is real; collect the real and the imaginary terms:

\[ \left({{CT:4}}+{{CT:7}}\right)+\left({{CT:6}}-{{CT:5}}\right)i={{CT:13}} \]

Step 3 — Divide
Divide the real part and the imaginary part by the real denominator, and reduce the fractions:

\[ \frac{{{CT:14}}}{{{CT:12}}}={{CT:15}} \]

that is, \(p={{CT:16}}\) and \(q={{CT:17}}\):

\[ \frac{{{CT:0}}+{{CT:1}}i}{{{CT:2}}+{{CT:3}}i}={{CT:18}} \]

on_true.feedback: The real part of your answer is correct.
The imaginary part of your answer is correct.
Your answer is equivalent to the correct answer, but not in the required form \(p + qi\).
